value.body: Structural engineers design and check the frames, beams, columns and foundations that keep buildings, bridges and other structures safe. They work in design consultancies, construction firms and government departments, and the day is mostly analysis and design on software, checking drawings and coordinating with architects and site teams.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech in Civil Engineering; usually M.Tech in Structural Engineering

items.label: Common tools
items.value: STAAD.Pro, ETABS, AutoCAD, Indian Standard codes (IS 456, IS 800, IS 1893)

items.label: GATE Civil Engineering paper
items.note: The usual route to an M.Tech in structural engineering

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Many structural design firms prefer an M.Tech in structural engineering, often reached through GATE. B.Tech graduates also start as trainee design engineers or move from site work into design after gaining experience.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Design of RCC and steel members to IS codes
Understanding loads, including earthquake and wind

value.title: At a glance
items: Design firms often hire in small numbers.
Common next steps: senior design engineer, design lead or proof consultant.
Signing drawings for approvals may need registration with a local authority.
